newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa called to open $15-$20 per tonne lower.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa called to open $15-$20 per tonne lower.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures were called to open $15 to $20 lower Wednesday in line with losses overnight in London, traders said.
LIFFE cocoa futures slumped early Wednesday, pressured by fund long liquidation. July cocoa was down 15 stg at the midday break at 1,002 stg a tonne, just shy of key chart support at 1,000 stg.

Tuesday, New York cocoa futures ended tightly mixed as traders focused on rolling over and liquidating July ahead of delivery period in two weeks. July settled unchanged at $1,449 a tonne after ranging from $1,458 to $1,441. September rose $3 to $1,488, while the back months fell $1.

With July open interest at 26,820 lots as of June 2 and only two weeks to go until the spot contract enters delivery period on June 17, traders expected the market to remain under pressure as speculators continue to liquidate or rollover Julys.

Technically, traders said July may find initial support near $1,440-$1,439, with a major downside hurdle seen at $1,425. Resistance was seen at $1,465-$1,467. ((--Patricia Avidan, New York Commodity Desk 212 859 1640))
